messages.subject: speed function
parts:
Dear Chris,

I am working with GPS data from bats that has no calibration data, therefore I am using 20 m as error. I am trying to calculate speed and distance from 14 individuals that have data between 2-3 days during only 2 hours every day. My GPS fixes were every 30 seconds and I have gaps of 24 hours between days.

I am trying to run a loop for all individuals, but first I am checking only one individual to see if the loop and the functions work. When I am calculating the speed, I am facing an error of unused arguments. The error says:
"Error in speed (object = data.subset, CTMM = fit, units = FALSE):
   unused arguments (object = data.subset, CTMM = fit, units = FALSE)"
 
I have updated the ctmm package but that didn't seem to work.

Here is my for loop:

level <- c(0.5,0.95) # 50% and 95% CIs
dt=c(0.5, 1440) %#% "minutes"
vg_all <- lapply(1:14, function(i) variogram(bachelors.tele[[i]],dt=dt))

res=c()
speeds=c()
count=1
PROTO=ctmm(error=20)
for(i in 1:14){
  days=unique(as.numeric(cut(bachelors.tele[[i]]$timestamp,breaks="24 hours")))
  bachelors.tele[[i]]$day=as.numeric(cut(bachelors.tele[[i]]$timestamp,breaks="24 hours"))
  print(bachelors.tele[[i]]@info$identity)
  try(for(j in 1:length(days)){
    #select data for day#
    possibleError=tryCatch({
    data.subset=bachelors.tele[[i]][which(bachelors.tele[[i]]$day==days[j]),]
    date=as.character(as.Date(data.subset$timestamp[1]))
    message("estimating distance traveled on day",j,":",date)
    ID=bachelors.tele[[i]]@info$identity
    samp.time=diff(c(data.subset$t[1],data.subset$t[nrow(data.subset)]))
    guess=ctmm.guess(bachelors.tele[[i]],CTMM=PROTO,variogram=vg_all[[i]],interactive=FALSE)
    fit=ctmm.fit(data.subset,CTMM=guess,method="pHREML",control=list(method="pNewton",cores=-1))
    ctmm_speed=speed(object=data.subset,CTMM=fit,units=FALSE)
    ctmm_dist=ctmm_speed*samp.time
    print(ctmm_dist[2])
    rownames(ctmm_dist)="distance(meters)"
    x=c(days[j],ctmm_dist[2],ctmm_dist[1],ctmm_dist[3],date,ID)
    names(x)=c("day","ctmm.estimate","ctmm.min","ctmm.max","date","ID")
    res[count]=list(x)
    count=count+1
    },error=function(e)e)
    if(inherits(possibleError,"error"))next
  })
}
speeds=do.call(rbind,res)
speeds=as.data.frame(speeds)

This is the result from my fit variable from one individual during only one day. I don't know if the problem might be there, or in the speed function.

> summary(fit)
$name
[1] "OUF anisotropic error"

$DOF
     mean      area          speed 
3.8026090 4.3509714 0.2577695 

$CI
                                                  low        est        high
area (square kilometers) 0.5349043   1.830906    3.909759
τ[position] (minutes)    0.2661481  20.504285 1579.668323
τ[velocity] (seconds)    0.0000000   3.402670   17.139316
speed (kilometers/day)   0.8465318 668.414728 1739.806758
error (meters)           3.2955992  10.997445   18.983570

Any guess of what could be happening ?
Thanks a lot for your help.
best,

Camila

messages.author: b7aff788b6a63d16
messages.subject: Re: speed function
parts:
Hey Chris,

I found the problem. Now the speed function works, but I had to write it like this: ctmm::speed. Somehow it conflicts with other functions with the same name.

cheers,
Camila

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: speed function
parts:
Hi Camila,

I'm guessing that you had another package loaded (maybe move ?) with a function of the same name. I'd suggest either only loading the packages you need, and using package::function() for rare calls from a package, or doing what you did and using package::function() for conflicting function names. This also happens a lot with plot(), even though we all share the same generic function.

Best,
Chris
